slides.title: TEMPA
slides.subtitle: The label that existed before dubstep had a name.
slides.image_concept: Pure white vinyl label on black record, close-up, dark background
slides.image_keywords: vinyl record white label dark background close-up

slides.text:
London, 2000.
Neil Jolliffe and Sarah Lockhart founded Tempa Recordings.
The first release: Horsepower Productions —
a UK garage sound stripped of warmth.
The genre didn't have a name yet.
slides.image_concept: South London street at night, residential, thin fog, narrow alley
slides.image_keywords: south london night street residential fog 2000s

slides.text:
2001. FWD>> opened.
Every week. Same room.
Hatcha brought tapes of teenagers from Croydon.
Nobody knew what to call the sound.
slides.image_concept: Dark club interior, minimal lighting, DJ booth in the distance, silhouettes of crowd
slides.image_keywords: dark club interior DJ booth silhouette crowd

slides.text:
2002. Four people in a conversation —
Neil Jolliffe, Sarah Lockhart, Oris Jay, Martin Clark.
One word came out: 'Dubstep.'
XLR8R magazine printed it on the cover.
slides.image_concept: Close-up of a single bold word in print, typewriter or magazine typography

slides.text:
June 2003.
Dubstep AllStars Vol. 1 — mixed by Hatcha.
The first release to print the word on a sleeve.
It was still a secret.
slides.image_concept: 12-inch vinyl record sleeve, label text barely visible, dark and close
slides.image_keywords: vinyl record sleeve label detail dark

slides.text:
2005. Skream. 'Midnight Request Line.'
A chord change that shouldn't have worked.
It worked.
Tempa's biggest release. Still is.
slides.image_concept: Turntable needle dropping onto vinyl record, extreme close-up
slides.image_keywords: turntable needle vinyl record drop close-up

slides.text:
2008. Benga. 'Diary of an Afro Warrior.'
19 tracks. Coki. Digital Mystikz.
The genre's peak, contained in 12 inches.
Tempa had built the container.
slides.image_concept: Record shop vinyl rack, hand pulling out a 12-inch sleeve
slides.image_keywords: record shop 12 inch vinyl rack hand pulling

slides.text:
Tempa named the sound.
Tempa housed the sound.
The sound outlived the name.

Save this.
